content: The six delinquent officials would face charge sheets and another 21 polling officials shall face disciplinary proceedings, the poll body said in a letter issued to the Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh.

content: Asserting that all decisions are unanimous, the Commission said the petitions on the matter filed in the top court are based solely on newspaper reports and should be dismissed.

content: The verification drive could change the size of the beneficiary list, making the latest figures important for understanding how the scheme has evolved and what may change next.

title: Several Workers Trapped In Bengal Coal Mine After Pulley System Glitch
content: Eastern Coalfields Ltd (ECL) CMD Satish Jha said the incident happened at the Kumardihi A underground mine after a rope slipped off the pulley drum, disrupting the mechanism used to transport workers in the cage.

title: A "Final" Warning For Protesting Students As Jamia Extends Online Classes
content: The notice, shared by the protesters, said their presence in the building, which houses the departments of Political Science and Economics, was unlawful and disrupting academic activities.

title: Microsoft extends buyouts to 60,000 staff in India, US, UK and Canada
content: Microsoft is offering buyouts to around 60,000 employees in India, the US, the UK and Canada under a new Voluntary Exit Offer, announced in a memo from Chief People Officer Amy Coleman. Open up to level 70, the offer has no age, tenure or performance criteria and mirrors standard severance. Employees have until early December to decide. The move follows 4,800 Microsoft layoffs in July.

title: Texas couple lose 70-acre family land after mother excludes son from her will
content: A Texas couple have lost their legal battle to remain on 70 acres of land they say had been in their family for decades. The dispute began after William Dan Moss was excluded from his mother's will. Despite challenging the inheritance decision and subsequent eviction, William and his wife, Brenda, failed to overturn the rulings. On October 22, a Texas appeals court upheld the eviction judgment.

title: Anbil Mahesh arrested; high drama precedes his remand
content: A CCB team reached his apartment in Aminjikarai and arrested him after Madras high court dismissed his anticipatory bail application.

title: Chris Hemsworth bought A$7m estate, rebuilt it with 50m pool and bike track
content: In a bold move away from Hollywood's hustle, Chris Hemsworth and Elsa Pataky have turned a coastal property in Byron Bay into a stunning modern mansion. The residence boasts a breathtaking 50-meter infinity pool, a fully equipped gym, and expansive outdoor areas for leisure. Recent upgrades include a tennis court and a dirt-bike track, enhancing the estate's allure.

title: Started for kids in 1969, Alaska family's mini railway now spans 3.5 miles
content: In Wasilla, Alaska, a charming miniature railway stretches 3.5 miles, proudly family-run since 1969. This enchanting railroad features tunnels, bridges, and whimsical scale-model towns, captivating visitors of all ages. As a nonprofit organization, it thrives on volunteer support, offering memorable train rides, including a special chair car for those with special needs. Donations and volunteer efforts are vital for its ongoing maintenance and potential expansions.

title: Bill Gates says Meta’s Muse is the first great consumer AI product, but has one worry
content: Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates has called Meta's Muse "the first truly great consumer AI product" in an interview with The Verge, revealing he congratulated chief AI officer Alexandr Wang on the personal AI agent. Gates said Muse stands out because it actually gets tasks done, but warned that open-weight AI models with removable safeguards are irresponsible, a week after Meta released its own Muse Spark Open.

title: Michigan court overturns $1.55m judgment against couple in home sale dispute
content: A Michigan appeals court has made headlines by overturning a hefty judgment against a couple who backed out of purchasing a luxury residence. Following an inspection that unveiled critical defects, the couple tried to renegotiate the price but ended up facing a breach of contract lawsuit. The trial court had favored the sellers, but the appeals court clarified the buyers' rights regarding inspection clauses, ultimately nullifying the ruling.

title: CSK clear decks for Zaheer-led reset; part ways with Hussey, old support staff
content: Hussey, who joined CSK as batting coach in 2018 after playing six seasons for the franchise, will not continue in the role from IPL 2027.

title: The Rock’s $800M fortune: How Dwayne Johnson built his global empire
content: Dwayne Johnson has taken his wrestling fame and turned it into a global entertainment and business empire spanning Hollywood, production, consumer brands and real estate. Years of strategic career choices have taken him from WWE superstar to one of the world’s most recognizable entertainers. Johnson is married to Lauren Hashian, and he juggles family life with big projects outside the wrestling ring and movie sets.

title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million estate faces new setback as neighbors object
content: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion faces fresh delays as neighbors challenge his landscaping and fencing plans. Residents have raised concerns about wildlife safety, lake views and potential damage to an aging sewer line, with one neighbor citing $75,000 in repair costs. Kelce’s construction team says it has spent $7,500 on sewer repairs and adjusted the plans. However, local officials require further changes before the remaining landscaping work can proceed.

title: 'Who checks the power?' Ex-SC judge calls for safeguards in poll panel appointments
content: Justice Abhay Oka presented compelling arguments for a structured legal framework to ensure election commissioners' independence. He cited Lal Krishna Advani's collegium system as a potential method for their selection. Oka placed strong emphasis on civil discourse as a pillar of democracy and raised alarms about environmental issues fueling rising temperatures in urban areas like Thane and Mumbai. Additionally, he recommended more efficient uses for public transport funding.

title: Can the man Trump called a 'jihadist' become America's first Muslim senator?
content: Donald Trump has called Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed a "jihadist" and accused him of extremist links without evidence. As El-Sayed faces Republican Mike Rogers in a closely contested race, can he overcome the controversy to become America's first Muslim senator?

title: Saudi Arabia turns to AI system to hunt Houthi missiles; why it may not be effective
content: Saudi Arabia is utilizing artificial intelligence to improve its military response to Houthi missile operations. The US military’s Maven Smart System aids in detecting potential threats and identifying targets quickly. Despite its advantages, challenges remain due to the Houthis’ mobile tactics and rugged terrain. Concerns over civilian casualties and targeting errors further complicate the operation's effectiveness. Increased efficiency may not guarantee a decisive victory in this ongoing conflict.

title: Kolkata: Teen caught kissing 13-year-old girlfriend, paraded naked along with father
content: An 18-year-old boy, along with his father and friend, faced a shocking assault in Kolkata after he was caught kissing his underage girlfriend. The girl's family allegedly threatened them and forced the couple to parade without clothes. This incident sparked outrage among local residents, leading to vandalism at the suspects' home and clashes with police forces. Authorities have since arrested three individuals, including the girl's parents and uncle.

title: 'Travesty': SC flays UP Police for 'slipshod probe' in murder case, orders reparation
content: The Supreme Court of India has ruled that the Uttar Pradesh government must compensate a man with Rs 6 lakh after he spent six years as an undertrial in a serious murder charge. The court condemned the shoddy investigative practices of the state police and prosecution, leading to his wrongful incarceration.

title: Anthropic IPO: Losses, dividends & risks to humanity; what investors should know
content: Anthropic, founded by ex-OpenAI employees, seeks to list on Nasdaq despite significant financial losses. The company's recent filing reveals a staggering net loss of $80.7 billion in 2026, with no dividends expected for investors. As it focuses on AI technology, potential risks to humanity are highlighted in their disclosure. The founders have substantial shares, creating uncertainty around their post-IPO ownership and plans.

title: ‘Hid previous marriage’: Father accuses husband of murder after woman dies at hotel
content: In a devastating turn of events, Ramji Lal Ahirwar accuses his son-in-law, Nilesh, of murdering his beloved daughter, Muskan Simolia. Allegedly, Nilesh's deception about his previous marriage led to severe distress for Muskan, culminating in her unexpected collapse at a hotel. Authorities have moved swiftly, apprehending Nilesh for interrogation while they unravel the facts of the case. A postmortem is anticipated to reveal the truth behind Muskan's tragic death.

title: Australia press panic button ahead of third Test; release opener, Smith uncertain
content: Maddinson and back-up wicketkeeper Sam Harper have been allowed to return to Australia to play in the Sheffield Shield, with Cameron Green and Josh Inglis fit again and available for selection.

title: Israel elections: Can Netanyahu turn security gains into a political victory?
content: Israeli voters will head to the polls on October 27 in a significant election for Benjamin Netanyahu. His political future hinges on addressing security failures following the October 7 attack by Hamas. Gadi Eisenkot has emerged as a primary challenger, emphasizing military accountability over Netanyahu's leadership. The election highlights divisions within the opposition and potential coalition challenges.

title: Nuclear-capable Rafales: Inside France's 'Forward Deterrence' plan to check Russia
content: France is pursuing a strategy called 'Forward Deterrence' to enhance its nuclear presence in Europe, which includes its Rafale jets. This initiative aims to deploy nuclear-capable aircraft to allied countries and bolster military cooperation. As the US urges NATO allies for increased defense spending, concerns arise over its commitment to European security.

title: Ronaldo sold his 90% Cruzeiro stake in 2024 and bought a $7.8M Miami penthouse
content: In 2026, Brazilian football legend Ronaldo Nazário reportedly purchased a $7.8 million waterfront duplex penthouse at Onda Residences in Miami’s Bay Harbor Islands. The acquisition followed his exits from Brazilian club Cruzeiro in 2024 and Spanish side Real Valladolid in 2025. Featuring five bedrooms, a private rooftop pool and panoramic Biscayne Bay views, the property reflects his strategic shift toward luxury real estate investment.

title: Zepto charged Rs 34 above MRP; consumer court ordered them to pay Rs 57,000
content: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission found Zepto charged more than the maximum retail price for groceries. Advocate K Shiva Ganesh filed a complaint regarding inflated prices on Zepto's platform. The commission determined that this practice was misleading and constituted unfair trade. Zepto was directed to compensate the complainant and deposit funds into the legal aid account. The company was also instructed to discontinue such practices in the future.

title: 'Stand near a powerful fan': India coach's unique advice to players ahead of Test
content: India will play a two-match Test series against New Zealand after the ongoing T20I and ODI series. The first Test is scheduled to begin at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on November 18.

title: 82-foot whale made from 5,000lb of plastic named Roadside America sight of week
content: Ethyl the Whale, an impressive 82-foot sculpture, currently resides at Santa Fe Community College in New Mexico. Designed by artists Joel Dean Stockdill and Yustina Salnikova, this monumental piece is crafted from approximately 5,000 pounds of discarded plastic. It draws attention to the crisis of ocean pollution and showcases how art can be born from trash, serving as a vital monument for sustainability and environmental awareness.

title: Why used cars just below round mileage figures fetch up to $168 more
content: A recent study showed that used car dealers profit from mileage readings just under round-number thresholds. The researchers analyzed millions of transactions to determine pricing impacts of left-digit bias. Buyers often overlook minor differences in mileage, focusing instead on the first digit. This inattention allows dealers to charge more for cars that appear to be better value.

title: Defence boost: Govt clears mega Rs 2.12 lakh crore acquisition deal; who gets what
content: On October 26, the Defence Acquisition Council has given the green light for a substantial military funding initiative totaling Rs 2.12 lakh crore. The focus lies on enhancing the capabilities of the Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force. Notably, about 82 percent of these procurements are anticipated to be sourced from domestic producers, thereby fostering local manufacturing.

title: 'Rising runoff, flood risks': Fresh warning over China’s mega Brahmaputra dam
content: Chinese researchers highlight potential increases in runoff and flood risks for the Brahmaputra River this century. Their study uses tree-ring data to model future climate scenarios affecting runoff. The implications of the $168 billion mega dam project in Tibet raise concerns for downstream countries like India and Bangladesh. Researchers urge careful planning of water-resource infrastructure to mitigate risks associated with international river management.

content: ICE has announced the removal of a 45-year-old man wanted in his home country for an alleged 2015 murder . Kanand Ojha was wanted by Guyanese police over the killing of Nephi Noel in Georgetown, the south american country's capital .

title: Missouri teen shot dead on way to Halloween party; suspect tied to 2nd shooting

title: SC restores Karnataka land, says government can acquire only for public purpose
content: govt can acquire land from citizens only for public purpose and not for the benefit of some person or organisation . a bench of justices held that the whole process of land acquisition is indicating "the fraud played on unsuspecting citizens" it said that illegal acquisitions were made through fraud and undue influence .

title: ‘Concrete measures’: Macron seeks to quell France’s student unrest
content: the government is expected to announce changes to parcoursup . students have criticised its selection criteria, arguing that they lack transparency and limit equal access to preferred courses . the government will announce concrete measures after weeks of protests, school blockades and demonstrations continue to fuel unrest .

title: Parliaments can serve as bridges to ease global tensions, says Birla
content:
File photo: Parliaments could be bridges of understanding, ease international tensions: Om Birla

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla said on Monday that parliaments as expressions of the people’s will could serve as bridges to ease international tensions at a time of global uncertainty, heightened by regional conflicts, wars, terrorism and trade disruptions, and called on Brics legislatures to foster collective action. Inaugurating the 12th Brics Parliamentary Forum, he said the consequences of geopolitical and economic headwinds transcended national boundaries and must be met with a spirit of collective responsibility. “These shared aspirations provided a strong foundation for deeper engagement and purposeful cooperation. The Brics Parliamentary Forum must therefore emerge as a dynamic platform for building confidence, fostering understanding and advancing collective action in pursuit of these common goals,” the LS Speaker added.

End of Article
